source.title_on_document: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching

supplement.where: No separately designated supplement or appendix is stated. Figures 13 and 14 and Table 1 follow the references on PDF pp. 17-18 and were read as part of the full document.

paper_design_summary: A formative exchange with seven professional product designers informed the Inkspire system (p. 4, Section 3). In the main within-person study, twelve participants, six professional designers and six novices, completed lamp and chair design tasks using Inkspire and baseline ControlNet; tool and task order were counterbalanced, but random assignment to orders is not stated (pp. 7-8, Sections 5.1 and 5.3.2). The authors analyzed participant questionnaires on creativity support and final design quality, interaction logs, and semantic similarity of prompts; they did not report independent creativity ratings of the produced designs (pp. 8-11, Sections 5.2 and 6.1-6.3).

studies.label: Main within-subjects user study: Inkspire versus ControlNet

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each participant completed one design task with Inkspire and another with baseline ControlNet. Tool order and task order were counterbalanced; the method of allocating participants to sequences is not stated.
assignment.quote: We counterbalance both the order of the tools and the order of the design tasks.

arms.name: Inkspire
arms.description: Analogical inspirations, sketch-guided image generation after each stroke, and generated sketch-scaffold underlays. The same twelve participants also used ControlNet (pp. 7-8, Sections 5.1 and 5.3.2).

arms.name: Baseline ControlNet
arms.description: Prompt box and sketching canvas with manual generation; no analogical inspirations, scaffold underlays, or stroke-by-stroke generation (p. 18, Figure 14). The same twelve participants also used Inkspire (pp. 7-8, Sections 5.1 and 5.3.2).

participants.who: Six professional designers who perform product design daily or weekly and six novices with moderate drawing experience who do not actively engage in product design; recruited through known contacts and Upwork. The condition counts refer to the same people, not separate groups.
participants.quote: We invited twelve participants (P1-P12, 10 male and 2 female) to participate in a one-hour user study.
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 5.1 (Participants); p. 8, Section 5.3.2 and paired analyses in Section 6.1; p. 14, Section 7.1 explicitly reports n=12

ai_tool.name_model: Inkspire (GPT-4 and ControlNet-guided Stable Diffusion); baseline ControlNet
ai_tool.how_used: Inkspire uses GPT-4 to propose analogical inspirations and ControlNet-guided Stable Diffusion to generate designs from sketches, then converts generated designs to sketch-scaffold underlays for further iteration. The baseline uses manually entered prompts and sketches without these added features (pp. 5-7, Sections 4.2-4.3 and 5; p. 18, Figure 14).

task.description: Design a lamp with the theme of serenity and a chair with the theme of fluidity, completing one task with each tool; both tool order and task order were counterbalanced (p. 8, Section 5.3.2).
task.duration: 45 minutes for the design-task phase within a one-hour study (p. 8, Section 5.3.2; p. 7, Section 5.1).

outcomes.name: Self-reported exploration support (Creativity Support Index; 7-point Likert scale)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Inkspire: mean=5.83, SD=1.27; baseline ControlNet: mean=3.83, SD=1.64; paired t(11)=3.94, p<0.01, r=0.77, d_s=1.13. This is a participant rating of tool support for exploration, not an output creativity score.

outcomes.name: Self-reported inspiration support (Creativity Support Index; 7-point Likert scale)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Inkspire: mean=5.92, SD=1.24; baseline ControlNet: mean=4.00, SD=1.41; paired t(11)=3.44, p<0.01, r=0.72, d_s=0.99. This is a participant rating of tool support for inspiration, not an output creativity score.

outcomes.name: Self-rated final design quality (7-point Likert scale)
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Inkspire: mean=5.92, SD=1.08; baseline ControlNet: mean=4.58, SD=1.93; paired t(11)=2.11, p=0.06, r=0.54, d_s=0.61. The paper reports that the difference was not statistically significant; participants rated their own creations.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Section 6.3; p. 13, Figure 11 (left); p. 8, Section 5.2 identifies the raters as the participants

studies.label: Formative exchange with professional product designers

assignment.what_was_assigned: No comparative conditions or allocation to AI assistance are described; the designers participated in a formative exchange about their existing design practices.
assignment.quote: To understand how professional designers use Text-to-Image (T2I) models in their work, we conducted a day-long exchange session with a team of seven professional product designers from a large automotive company.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 3 (Formative Session with Design Professionals)

participants.who: Professional product designers at a large automotive company, spanning creative direction, modeling, interior and exterior design, artistic and conceptual creation, and UX/UI and strategy. Their exchange informed the system design; this is not the main comparative sample.
participants.quote: To understand how professional designers use Text-to-Image (T2I) models in their work, we conducted a day-long exchange session with a team of seven professional product designers from a large automotive company.

ai_tool.name_model: Midjourney and Vizcom (reported prior experience; versions not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Designers showed their existing design processes and use of current text-to-image tools and discussed challenges; no assigned tool comparison is described (p. 4, Section 3).

task.description: Present prior design processes and examples, demonstrate existing text-to-image workflows, and discuss challenges and possible tool improvements; no creative-output scoring is reported (p. 4, Section 3).

company_involvement.description: Toyota Research Institute funded the work, and coauthors Yan-Ying Chen and Matthew K. Hong are affiliated with Toyota Research Institute. The acknowledgments also report funding from the Office of Naval Research.

eligibility.reason: The main comparison analyzed 12 people, below the 50-person threshold (p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 14, Section 7.1). The authors state that tool and task orders were counterbalanced but do not state random assignment to orders (p. 8, Section 5.3.2); this supports randomized=not_stated and design_class=other, rather than a confirmed randomized or explicitly non-randomized comparison. Creativity-support and final-design-quality scores are participant self-ratings (p. 8, Section 5.2; p. 11, Section 6.3). The computed BERTScore concerns user prompts, not scored creativity or diversity of the produced designs (p. 9, Section 6.2.2); interaction logs and qualitative observations do not supply a qualifying scored design outcome (pp. 10-11, Sections 6.2.3-6.3). The formative exchange involved seven designers but no comparison of assigned conditions or qualifying scored output (p. 4, Section 3), and is not combined with the main study for the participant threshold. Accordingly the paper is excluded from core and does not provide an eligible context comparison under the codebook.

one_line_finding: In the counterbalanced within-person study of 12 people (p. 7, Section 5.1), Inkspire increased self-reported exploration (mean=5.83 versus 3.83) and inspiration (mean=5.92 versus 4.00; both p<0.01; p. 8, Section 6.1), while self-rated final design quality did not differ significantly (mean=5.92 versus 4.58, p=0.06; p. 11, Section 6.3).
